name: Chip Fabrication
blurb: Who actually manufactures AI silicon, on what process, and where.

items.name: GlobalFoundries
items.note: Trailing-edge and specialty nodes; the US-based volume foundry for everything that does not need leading edge

items.name: Intel Foundry
items.note: Intel's external foundry business; 18A is its leading-edge node bid for AI silicon

items.name: Samsung Foundry
items.note: The second leading-edge logic foundry; gate-all-around SF3/SF2 nodes

items.name: SMIC
items.note: China's leading foundry and the fabrication path for domestic AI accelerators under export controls

items.name: TSMC
items.note: Fabricates nearly every leading AI accelerator - NVIDIA, AMD, Apple, Google TPU - on N5/N4/N3 nodes; corporate site bot-walls verification, so the source is its SEC 20-F filing index

reading.body:
Five companies make up this collection of AI chip fabrication, and TSMC is named as the manufacturer of nearly every leading AI accelerator, including chips for NVIDIA, AMD, Apple, and Google's TPU line, on its N5, N4, and N3 process nodes.

Intel Foundry and Samsung Foundry are described as the two other leading-edge logic foundries, competing at the newest process nodes, Intel with its 18A node bid for AI silicon and Samsung with gate-all-around SF3 and SF2 nodes, while GlobalFoundries is described as the trailing-edge and specialty node option for chips that do not require leading-edge manufacturing. SMIC is named separately as China's leading foundry and the fabrication path for domestic AI accelerators operating under export controls, a distinct role from the other four companies in this collection, none of which are described as constrained by export control regimes.

TSMC's entry notes that its own corporate site blocks automated verification, so this collection confirms TSMC's data through its SEC 20-F filing index instead, a different verification path than the other four fabs in this set, whose entries are each verified directly against a company or product page.
